analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR patch adds one table row at head line 1389, documenting `decodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks` as 4 for the Qwen 3.5 family and 0 otherwise. The supplied units (head lines 417-1215) are unchanged surrounding text, not part of the changed range, and I treated them as context only. The row does not appear in either unit; it sits outside the supplied excerpts and is visible only in the patch.

Security relevance: this scheduler knob interleaves decode-only steps between prefill chunks. It affects availability and latency only (T-010, T-029 are loosely related) and does not touch the encryption, attestation, authorization or at-rest paths. The retained cache threat T-041 is not affected. The unit text describes SSD prefix-cache checkpoints encrypted under the provider cache root, coordinator-authored cache scope partitioning, and KEK-rooted durability. All of this is consistent with T-041's posture: no raw prefix hashes on disk, a TTL-bounded cache, and scope folded into the lookup tag.

No code was supplied, so I cannot verify that the documented default of 4 for Qwen 3.5 matches `EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift` (`qwenDecodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`). That is a doc-accuracy question, not a security regression. A possible side effect is that the deadline projection and first-token latency shift for prefilling requests. That is a performance and routing matter owned by the platform. The new setting changes no trust boundary, secret handling, billing or authorization behavior. No threat model update is needed.
